## Authentication

Every request requires a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Keys start with `ipx_live_`.

HTTP

    // In your Express/Next.js handler:
    app.post("/webhook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => {
      const sig = req.headers["x-ipayx-signature"];
      if (!verifySignature(req.body, sig, process.env.IPAYX_WEBHOOK_SECRET)) {

# Logging In

To use the iPay API, you need a merchant account.

Account creation is handled by the iPay team. Contact support via i-pay.io to initiate the process. Accounts are opened after a simple KYB (website, incorporation documents, directors/shareholders/UBO), reviewed by the iPay team within 24 hours.

Once your account is approved, log in to the dashboard:

  1. Visit dash.i-pay.io and click “Forgot password”.
  2. Follow the emailed link to set a new password.
  3. Log in with your credentials.

After logging in, use the dashboard for initial setup:

  * Company Registration: Enter your business details.
  * Account Setup: Connect your crypto wallet.
  * API Key Creation: Generate a key with your callback URL, then have the iPay team activate it and register your redirect URL.

Keep credentials secure and share dashboard access only with trusted team members.

# Creating an API Key

With a company and account configured, create an API Key to link your integration components.

Go to the API Key Menu --> 🗝

  1. Select your Account from the dropdown
  2. Enter your callback URL for HTTP POST notifications. --> Click on the Request button to complete

The system generates a unique API key.

important

Reach out to the iPay Team either directly, or via [email protected] to activate your API key.

When you do, also provide your redirect URL — the page on your site where the customer should land after completing the payment (e.g. your deposit-success or dashboard page). The iPay team registers it together with your API key.

## Callback URL vs. redirect URL​

 | Callback URL (IPN)  | Redirect URL
--- | --- | ---
Who calls it  | iPay server → your server (HTTP POST, JSON)  | The customer's browser, after the payment is completed
Purpose  | Credit the deposit in your system  | Close the customer journey — show a confirmation page
Trust it for crediting?  | Yes — this is the source of truth  | No — a page load can be reached without a completed payment
Where it is set  | Dashboard, when requesting the API key  | Registered by the iPay team when activating the key

Your redirect page should simply thank the customer and show the pending/credited status from your own records — the credit itself must come from the HTTP POST callback.

# iPayX Protocol — Neutral FX Verification Layer

iPayX Protocol is the neutral FX verification layer for fintech sales teams and FX brokers. We audit foreign-exchange transactions, compare the rate a bank or card network applied against the real-time mid-market rate, reveal invisible spreads, quantify FX costs, and project annual savings.

## How It Works

  1. Enter your transaction – Amount, currencies (e.g. CAD → USD), and the rate your bank applied.
  2. We capture the mid-market rate – From regulated interbank data sources at the exact transaction time.
  3. Instant audit report – Spread %, FX cost in your base currency, execution grade (A/B/C), and annual savings projection.

# Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I obtain an API key?

A: Log in to the iPay dashboard, navigate to the API Keys section, and create a new key with your company, wallet, and callback URL. Then contact the iPay team to activate it — they will also register your redirect URL at this point.

Q: What is the redirect URL?

A: The page on your site where the customer lands after completing the payment (e.g. your deposit-success or dashboard page). It is registered by the iPay team when your API key is activated. It only closes the customer journey — never credit a deposit based on the redirect; credit it when the server-to-server callback arrives.

Q: What happens if my callback URL is down?

A: iPay may retry sending the notification. Ensure your endpoint is reliable and logs errors for debugging.

Q: Can I use multiple wallets?

A: Yes, add multiple wallets in the dashboard and create separate API keys for each.

Q: How do I verify the secret token?

A: Compare the `authorization` HTTP header of the callback request with the secret token provided by iPay. Reject mismatches. The token is not part of the JSON body.

Q: Why are some callback fields spelled unusually?

A: The callback sends `transferedAmount` (single r) and `transactionFeePrecent` exactly as written. Match these keys literally in your parser — see the JSON Payload Explanation.

For more questions, contact [email protected].
